draft.title: Isomers
card: Isomers are compounds with the same molecular formula but different structural arrangements of atoms. Different structures mean different properties.
Chain isomers
the carbon skeleton is arranged differently, such as a straight chain and a branched chain. Butane and 2-methylpropane are both C4H10.
Position isomers
the carbon skeleton is the same, but a double bond or other group sits at a different place. But-1-ene and but-2-ene are both C4H8.
Functional group isomers
the atoms form different functional groups. Ethanol and methoxymethane are both C2H6O, one with an OH group and one with an ether link.
draft.remember: Isomers share a molecular formula but differ in how the atoms are joined.

a.q: Which pair are isomers of each other?
a.why: Butane and 2-methylpropane are both C4H10 but have different structures. Propane (C3H8) and propene (C3H6) have different molecular formulas, so they are not isomers even though their names look similar.
a.clue: First check that the molecular formulas match.

b.q: Pent-1-ene and pent-2-ene both have the formula C5H10. Both have a straight five-carbon chain, but the double bond is in a different place. What type of isomers are they?
b.why: The carbon skeleton is the same and only the position of the double bond differs, so they are position isomers. Chain isomers would need a different carbon skeleton, such as a branched chain.
b.clue: Look at what stays the same and what moves.

problems.detail: The stem says the chain is the same and only the double bond's place differs. This restates the card's definition of position isomers almost word for word, so it gives the answer away instead of testing whether the student can recognise the structures.

b.q: What type of isomers are CH2=CHCH2CH2CH3 and CH3CH=CHCH2CH3?
b.why: Both are C5H10 with an unbranched chain of five carbons, so the skeleton is the same. The double bond starts at carbon 1 in one and carbon 2 in the other, so they are position isomers. Chain isomers would need a different skeleton, such as a branched chain.
b.clue: Count the carbons, hydrogens and chain shape in each first.
